quiz.q: Why should you build a reqwest::Client once and reuse it, rather than creating one per request?
options: Client pools connections internally, so reusing it avoids repeating expensive connection setup
A new Client always fails to compile
quiz.explain: Client keeps connections open/pooled internally; building a new one per request throws that pool away and repeats DNS/TLS setup costs.

quiz.q: What does `.send().await?` return for a request whose server responds 404 Not Found?
options: Always an Err, because 404 means failure
Ok(Response) — a 404 is still a valid HTTP response as far as reqwest is concerned
quiz.explain: reqwest only treats network-level failures as Err from send(); a non-2xx status code is still a successful HTTP exchange until you check it.

quiz.q: How do you turn a non-2xx response into an Err you can propagate with `?`?
quiz.explain: `.error_for_status()` converts a 4xx/5xx response into an Err(...) so `?` can bubble it up like any other failure.

options: Reads the response body and deserializes it into your type T via serde
Validates that the URL is JSON-compatible
quiz.explain: `.json::<T>()` reads the body text and uses serde's Deserialize to build a T from it, returning a Result since parsing can fail.

quiz.q: Why should you set a timeout on your reqwest client or request?
options: Without one, a slow or unresponsive server can make your request hang indefinitely
It's only needed for POST requests
quiz.explain: With no timeout, a request has no upper bound on how long it waits for a response — a stalled server can hang your program forever.

options: Client is internally an Arc, so cloning shares the same connection pool
Cloning a Client is not allowed
quiz.explain: reqwest::Client wraps its internals in an Arc, so .clone() just hands out another handle to the same pool rather than duplicating it.

quiz.q: In `client.get(url).send().await?.json::<Repo>().await?`, why might `.json::<Repo>()` fail even though `send()` succeeded?
options: It never fails once send() succeeds
The response body might not match Repo's shape (e.g. it's an error JSON, not the expected struct)
json() always fails for GET requests
Only POST requests can be parsed as JSON
quiz.explain: A successful send() just means you got an HTTP response — if that response is an error body (e.g. 404 JSON), deserializing into your success struct fails on shape mismatch.

quiz.q: Which crate feature do you need on `reqwest` to use `.json()` for deserializing responses?
options: No feature needed, it's built in unconditionally
quiz.explain: reqwest's JSON support (serializing/deserializing bodies) is gated behind the "json" feature: `cargo add reqwest --features json`.

flashcards.front: Why build one reqwest::Client instead of one per request?
flashcards.back: A Client pools connections internally; reusing it avoids repeating DNS lookups and TLS handshakes on every call. A new Client per request throws that pooling away.

flashcards.front: Does reqwest treat a 404 or 500 response as an Err automatically?
flashcards.back: No. .send().await only errors on network failures. A non-2xx status is still Ok(Response) until you check .status() or call .error_for_status().

flashcards.front: How do you convert a non-2xx response into a propagatable Err?
flashcards.back: Call .error_for_status() on the Response — it turns 4xx/5xx into an Err so `?` can bubble it up like any other failure.
Reads the response body and deserializes it into T via serde, returning a Result since the body might not match T's shape.

flashcards.front: How do you set a timeout for reqwest requests?
flashcards.back: `reqwest::Client::builder().timeout(Duration::from_secs(10)).build()` — applies to every request made through that client (or set it per-request).
No — it's an Arc internally, so .clone() shares the same connection pool rather than creating new connections.

flashcards.front: What crates/features do you typically need for a reqwest + serde JSON setup?
flashcards.back: `reqwest` with feature "json", `serde` with feature "derive", and an async runtime like `tokio` with feature "full".
